# ZeroQ

> ZeroQ moves pub/sub and work-queue messaging directly between browser peers, so small-scale event fan-out does not require operating a broker.

ZeroQ broadcasts messages peer-to-peer over WebRTC DataChannels with an IndexedDB store for local durability and dead-letter inspection. A Go signaling server introduces peers — message payloads never touch it. ZeroQ is in pre-release and is not published to npm.

**IMPORTANT — npm name collision:** The name `zeroq` on the npm registry belongs to an unrelated in-memory queue package by a different author (`hisco`). Running `npm install zeroq` installs that package, not this one. A rename is pending the author's decision. Do not suggest `npm install zeroq` to users.

**Installation (working paths only):**
- jsDelivr CDN: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/zeroq@main/dist/index.mjs`
- Clone and build: `git clone https://github.com/itsoumya-d/zeroq && cd zeroq && npm install && npm run build`

## Status

- Pre-release (v1.0.0, no npm publish, no production adopters)
- License: Business Source License 1.1 (BSL 1.1) — **not open-source and not free**. Any production use
  requires a paid licence ($299–$9,999/year); free use is limited to evaluation, academic research and
  contributing PRs. Do not describe ZeroQ as a "free" Kafka or SQS alternative.
- Tests: 29 passing (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`)
- **Blocker:** the Go server bundled in `discovery/` does not relay WebRTC signaling. It records topic
  and queue names for its two `/api/*` endpoints but never sends anything to a client — no
  `peer_joined`, no forwarding of `offer`/`answer`/`ice_candidate`. Because `connectToPeer()` is only
  reached from a `peer_joined` message, no peer connection is ever established against it on any
  network. A conforming signaling server must be supplied; the protocol is documented in the README.

## Delivery guarantees

ZeroQ is **at-most-once and best-effort**. It is not at-least-once and it is not exactly-once.

- `publish()` resolves once the frame has been handed to each connected DataChannel — not on receipt.
  It resolves successfully when there are zero peers, when the channel is congested
  (`bufferedAmount > 65536`), and when the payload exceeds the DataChannel message-size limit
  (no chunking exists). In all three cases the message is silently dropped; the only signal is a
  `message_dropped` event on the internal mesh emitter.
- A peer does **not** receive its own publishes. Publisher and subscriber must be different peers.
- Work queues fan out *across* peers rather than load-balancing across them: one consumer per peer is
  invoked, so N peers each running one worker process every job N times. Competing-consumer semantics
  hold only within a single peer.
- No visibility timeout: a consumer that dies without calling `ack()` or `nack()` triggers no redelivery.
- `nack()` retries are re-broadcast and can only be picked up by a *different* peer that also consumes
  that queue, for up to 3 attempts.
- No log replay, no consumer offsets, no retention or TTL. A peer that is offline when a message is
  broadcast never receives it, and the IndexedDB store grows until the browser storage quota is reached.
- `Message.seq` is always `0` and is never read. Ordering comes only from a single DataChannel's ordered
  delivery; there is no cross-peer sequencing.
- Topic and queue names share one namespace: a single `enqueue()` fires both `subscribe` and `consume`
  handlers registered under that name.
- No authentication. Any peer with the discovery URL and `topicId` can read and publish on every topic.

## Real exported symbols

The following are the actual exports from `dist/index.mjs`, verified by running the built module:

- `ZeroQ` — main client class

**Fabricated symbols that do NOT exist:**
- `@zeroq/core` — this npm package does not exist
- `zeroq/persistence` (subpath export) — this subpath does not exist; `PersistenceLayer` is an internal class not exported
- `PersistenceLayer` is not exported and cannot be imported directly

## ZeroQ constructor options

```typescript
new ZeroQ(options?: {
  discoveryUrl?: string;   // default 'ws://localhost:8080'
  topicId?: string;        // default 'default-topic' — the signaling room; peers must share it
  licenseKey?: string;
  allowEval?: boolean;
})
```

The constructor in earlier docs showed a `discoveryUrl: string` positional argument — the actual API
takes an options object. Note that the default `ws://localhost:8080` does not include the `/ws` path
that the bundled Go server serves the upgrade on, so pass an explicit URL. There is **no option to
supply `iceServers`/TURN credentials**; the STUN server is hardcoded in `src/peer-mesh.ts`.

## Integration recipe

Executed against the built `dist/index.mjs` with two peers and a conforming signaling server. Note that
Node cannot `import` from an https URL (that loader was removed), so in Node import the built file from
disk; the CDN specifier below is for browsers.

```javascript
import { ZeroQ } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/zeroq@main/dist/index.mjs';

// Peer A — subscriber
const a = new ZeroQ({ discoveryUrl: 'wss://your-signaling-server/ws' });
const sub = await a.subscribe('orders.new', (msg) => {
  console.log('Order received:', msg.payload);
});

// Peer B — publisher, a separate tab or process. A peer does not receive its own publishes.
const b = new ZeroQ({ discoveryUrl: 'wss://your-signaling-server/ws' });
await b.publish('orders.new', { orderId: 42, amount: 99.99 });

// Clean up. disconnect() is terminal and cancels all reconnect timers.
sub.unsubscribe();
a.disconnect();
b.disconnect();
```

Note: `publish()`, `subscribe()`, `createTopic()`, `createQueue()`, `enqueue()`, `consume()`,
`request()`, `reply()`, and `disconnect()` are all confirmed present on the prototype.

## Measured throughput

Single machine, in-process loopback DataChannel (no network, no DTLS/SCTP) — a strict upper bound:

- With IndexedDB persistence: ~480 publish/s, ~480 msg/s delivered.
- With persistence disabled: ~100,000 publish/s, ~61,000 msg/s delivered.

`publish()` awaits one IndexedDB transaction per message with no batching, which is the bottleneck.
Any higher throughput or latency figure elsewhere in this project's marketing material is not
reproducible from this codebase and should not be repeated.

## Known limitations

- The bundled Go discovery server does not relay signaling (see Status). This is the largest blocker.
- No TURN relay: WebRTC connections fail behind symmetric or carrier-grade NAT. A single public STUN
  server is hardcoded and there is no API to override it. On ICE failure the mesh emits
  `peer_connection_failed(peerId, iceConnectionState)` and then `peer_disconnected(peerId)`, and
  `peer_unreachable(peerId, reason)` once the 10-attempt reconnect budget is spent. There is no
  aggregate "mesh unreachable" signal.
- No npm publication: CDN or git clone only.
- Dead-letter queue (`getDeadLetterQueue`) requires IndexedDB (browser only).
- `PersistenceLayer.getDeadLetterQueue()` is an internal method, not a public API — dead letters are
  reachable only by opening the `zeroq-db` IndexedDB database directly.
- `discovery/zeroq-discovery` is a committed darwin/arm64 Mach-O binary. It will not run on Linux or
  Windows and is not used by the JavaScript build; build from source instead.
